blocks.text: Now, my dear readers, listen to the narration further, When Delhi was being ruled by the Pathan emperor. How he invited Guru Nanak's wrath on himself, And how his reign was replaced by the Mughal rule. (1)
lines: Now, my dear readers, listen to the narration further,
When Delhi was being ruled by the Pathan emperor.
How he invited Guru Nanak's wrath on himself,
And how his reign was replaced by the Mughal rule.

blocks.text: Brahm Khan Lodhi1 was the ruler of Delhi at that time, Who fell on bad days during his reign. He ordered all the Sidhas, Saints and prophets to be arrested, And made them grind corn with the manually operated Chakkis2 . (2)
lines: Brahm Khan Lodhi1 was the ruler of Delhi at that time,
Who fell on bad days during his reign.
He ordered all the Sidhas,
Saints and prophets to be arrested,
And made them grind corn with the manually operated Chakkis2 .

blocks.text: He declared all of them as fraudulent exploiters of the masses, Since they had failed to demonstrate any kind of miracles. Then all the Muslim and the Hindu saints agreed unanimously, That Guru Nanak alone was capable of getting them released. (3)
lines: He declared all of them as fraudulent exploiters of the masses,
Since they had failed to demonstrate any kind of miracles.
Then all the Muslim and the Hindu saints agreed unanimously,
That Guru Nanak alone was capable of getting them released.

blocks.text: He alone could protect their dignity and honour, He alone could preserve the sanctity of their sacred robes. As everyone is not the bravest amongst a battery of armed troops, As every animal is not as brave as a lion in the whole forest. (4)
lines: He alone could protect their dignity and honour,
He alone could preserve the sanctity of their sacred robes.
As everyone is not the bravest amongst a battery of armed troops,
As every animal is not as brave as a lion in the whole forest.

blocks.text: Hearing their petition, Guru Nanak remarked smilingly, That all the saints and prophets were equally empowered. That they were unnecessarily giving him that credit, And assured them that everything would turn out well the next day. (5)
lines: Hearing their petition,
Guru Nanak remarked smilingly,
That all the saints and prophets were equally empowered.
That they were unnecessarily giving him that credit,
And assured them that everything would turn out well the next day.

blocks.text: Guru Nanak made all stone -wheeled chakis run automatically, And made all the debris-loaded baskets rise above the heads of labouring saints. As he protected the honour of their sacred robes, His fame and reputation spread far and wide. (6)
lines: Guru Nanak made all stone -wheeled chakis run automatically,
And made all the debris-loaded baskets rise above the heads of labouring saints.
As he protected the honour of their sacred robes,
His fame and reputation spread far and wide.

blocks.text: An elephant belonging to a gardener had died, Satguru Guru Nanak brought this dead elephant back to life.
Since this gardener used to provide food and shelter to the saints, He became worthy of Guru Nanak's grace for his acts of service. (7)
lines: Since this gardener used to provide food and shelter to the saints,
He became worthy of Guru Nanak's grace for his acts of service.

blocks.text: The emperor felt extremely offended after hearing about these events, He felt that this Hindu (Guru Nanak) had displayed magical feats. He ordered/proclaimed that Guru Nanak be turned out of Delhi, And He must not be allowed to enter Delhi again. (8)
lines: The emperor felt extremely offended after hearing about these events,
He felt that this Hindu (Guru Nanak) had displayed magical feats.
He ordered/proclaimed that Guru Nanak be turned out of Delhi,
And He must not be allowed to enter Delhi again.

blocks.text: Guru Nanak retorted that he would enter Delhi again and again, And predicted that another king would henceforth rule Delhi. Guru Nanak also predicted the end of Lodhi Dynasty's empire, And said that their royal writ would cease to run by 1878 (B.S.). (9)
lines: Guru Nanak retorted that he would enter Delhi again and again,
And predicted that another king would henceforth rule Delhi.
Guru Nanak also predicted the end of Lodhi Dynasty's empire,
And said that their royal writ would cease to run by 1878 (B.S.).

blocks.text: Thus Sri Guru Nanak inflicted his curse on him, And he died of gastroenterological disorder. And Delhi was occupied by the Mughal king, Who became a devout follower of Guru Nanak. (10)
lines: Thus Sri Guru Nanak inflicted his curse on him,
And he died of gastroenterological disorder.
And Delhi was occupied by the Mughal king,
Who became a devout follower of Guru Nanak.
